generated_from.description: Started by todo_sync.py init; items added by todo_sync.py add from open GitHub issues.

ranking_method.score: value / sqrt(cost), multiplied by (1 + unblock_bonus) when the item unblocks at least one item
tie_breakers: primary source type, where the primary source is sources[0]: gh_issue, then impl_stub, then research_folder
primary source ref: issue number ascending for gh_issue, otherwise the ref path in code-point order
primary source item text in code-point order (absent item sorts first)

impact_definitions.silent_wrong_output: A shipped path completes without error or warning and publishes a value or feature that is wrong under an established rule.
impact_definitions.data_correctness: Output or reference data can be wrong or ungoverned, but the correct value still needs a rule or decision to define it, a guard is missing, or the wrong value already surfaces with a warning or error.
impact_definitions.runtime_failure: A path raises or aborts on an input it accepts.
impact_definitions.dev_velocity: Tests, CI or developer tooling are slower, noisier or less trustworthy than they need to be; no output changes.
impact_definitions.maintainability: Structure, duplication, dead code, missing tests or latent defects that no current production path reaches; no output changes.
impact_definitions.docs_tooling: Documentation, research records, configuration or agent tooling outside the shipped paths.

severity_scale.1: Cosmetic or hygiene: renames, dead code, stale docs, a test gap for working or accepted behavior.
severity_scale.2: Debt with a concrete cost, a latent defect that no current path reaches, a missing guard, or a defect that needs a rare or optional input.
severity_scale.3: A wrong or failing result on a supported but uncommon input, or a defect a warning already surfaces.
severity_scale.4: Wrong published output on a common input of a production path, or a failure that blocks a supported workflow.
severity_scale.5: Crashes or corrupts a production path on its normal inputs.

ranking_method.notes: Each item's severity, impact, LoE and blast radius come from its source's triage. Ranking compares scores rounded to 4 decimals; the tie breakers apply in order, so ids and ranks are reproducible from the item fields alone.

items.title: pr-review: background execution via a saved workflow (Phases 1-3)
items.decision_question: Can a plugin ship a saved workflow, or must the pr-review skill write one under the consuming project's .claude/workflows/ (issue Q4)? The answer settles where the Phases 1-3 workflow lives before any of it is built.
items.summary: pr-review cannot fork like c-msg or pr-sum: Phase 2 fans out harness:pr-reviewer rows from the main session, a fork would break the per-row model floor, the Phase 5 sentinel binds to the session id, the bubble pause needs the developer and fixers write the shared tree. The issue proposes a saved workflow that runs capture, the reviewer fan-out and merge in the background and returns before amend; Phases 4-5 stay in the foreground. Checked: plugins/harness/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md has no context: key (frontmatter lines 2-5), unlike plugins/harness/skills/c-msg/SKILL.md:5-6 (context: fork, agent: harness:messenger); plugins/harness/hooks/check_phase5_sentinel.py:103 defines blocks_session(owner, session_id); plugins/harness/scripts/pr_review.py has no capture --json mode (its only --json is the gh pr view call at :333); dispatch_shape allows only parallel and inline in plugins/pr-review-watch/hooks/matrixRow.ts:15 and plugins/harness/schemas/pr_review_invocation_test_matrix.schema.json:57-61. Unverified: whether a workflow-launched agent inherits the parent's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (Q2) and whether anything else parses capture's printed rows (Q1).
items.proposed_change: Settle Q4 first. Then add a capture --json mode to pr_review.py (or build the rows from the plan.json slots capture already writes), ship the Phases 1-3 workflow (capture, parallel harness:pr-reviewer agents with each row's model, merge) that stops after merge, add a Background mode section to the pr-review SKILL.md naming amend as the resume point and Phases 4-5 as foreground, and add dispatch_shape "workflow" to matrixRow.ts DISPATCH_SHAPES and the invocation matrix schema enum. Leave the Phase 5 workflow extension for later.

blast_radius.reasoning: Touches the pr-review skill, its capture driver and the reviewer-stats row shape shared with the pr-review-watch mod; the foreground path stays as it is.

loe.reasoning: A new workflow script, a structured capture output, a skill section, a schema enum and mod change, plus probes of the workflow runtime (Q2, Q4).

items.why_ranked: Severity 2 dev_velocity: a foreground pr-review blocks the session through the reviewer fan-out; size L for a new workflow, a capture mode and a schema change.

close_candidates.recommended_action: Close as completed by PR #82 (commit 0ace6b6); the PR said "Refs #77", so GitHub did not close it. Output noise of the new skill is tracked separately in #88.

close_candidates.title: Add "auto-message" blocks for pre-determined change sets
close_candidates.evidence: Merge 66977e3 ("Merge pull request #90 from t968rs/auto-commit-msg") is on main (`git log --oneline main`). Its commit 948f23f ("Feature(commit-msg): add canned messages for pre-determined change sets", body "Refs #86, #87") takes the subset-of-patterns, plugin-fixed answer to the decision question: plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/canned_messages.py:22 defines LOOKUP as a Mapping[FrozenSet[str], str] of file patterns (globs such as TODO_Snapshot_*.md at :27) and :54 get_canned_message returns the message of the first entry covering every changed file; plugins/harness/scripts/branch_commit_msg.py:288-290 prefills an empty block from it during capture and :55-57 add the `canned` subcommand, which plugins/harness/skills/merge-commit-msg/SKILL.md:41 uses. 446823f follows up on the review; tests/lib/test_canned_messages.py and tests/skills/test_canned_message_skill_contract.py cover it. The commit said "Refs", so no closing keyword reached the issue.
close_candidates.recommended_action: Close as completed by PR #90 (commit 948f23f). Presets are fixed in the plugin, not configurable; open a new issue if per-project presets are wanted.

close_candidates.title: Add argument to `pr-sum` to include local changes
close_candidates.evidence: Merge 5ccdee9 ("Merge pull request #95 from t968rs/1077-pr-local") is on main (`git log --oneline main`). Its commit b2f8bc4 ("Feature(pr-sum): add --local capture of the checked-out branch") adds the opt-in flag the decision question asked about: plugins/harness/scripts/pr_sum.py:310 defines --local, which reads whatever HEAD is checked out from its merge base with the PR base to the working tree, exclusive with --remote-head; 6b563a8 labels --local checkouts by HEAD. The docs gap is closed too: plugins/harness/skills/pr-sum/SKILL.md:4 argument-hint now lists --local, --remote-head and --committed-only, and README.md:19 says the pr-sum row covers uncommitted changes and --local. tests/scripts/test_pr_sum.py covers forced local capture on another branch. The default working-tree capture on the PR branch predates the issue (18f883f, PR #34).
close_candidates.recommended_action: Close as completed by PR #95 (commits b2f8bc4, 6b563a8).
